It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as schoolteacher, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

By the winter of 1834-35 Andreas has George Davis opening a school on Lake Street over a store between Dearborn and Clark, and later in 1835 teaching in the Presbyterian church, which is a different man in a different room.

persons.name: Grenville Temple Sproat

occupation.note: 'The lower story was a hall for religious services, the upper floor was a school-room, where Granville Temple Sproat kept one of the first public schools.' The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 independently reports a school established in the village by Mr Sproat of Boston, already running on the day the paper appeared.

workplaces.basis: The register matches the printed name to the town card sproat_grenville (action: enrich), so this is the same person the resident layer already holds. Dated by the printing window, which bounds the reading and does not date the partnership.

persons.note: DOCUMENTED CONTEMPORANEOUSLY AND RETROSPECTIVELY, WITH AN ORIGIN IN THE CONTEMPORARY SOURCE - which makes this the only origin in the parcel that comes from a Chicago document rather than from a memoir. Andreas spells the forename both Granville and Grenville and the index carries 'Sproot, Grenville Temple'; his English and Classical School for Boys occupied the upper storey of the Temple Building. Two women are named as teachers in the same building at different times - 'Miss Chappel (Mrs. Jeremiah Porter), Miss Sarah Warren (Mrs. Abel E. Carpenter), and S. L. Carpenter' - and none of the three is written as a household here because none of them is placed in the town on any date near the scene date.

resident_research.evidence_for: Early education histories identify Granville T. Sproat opening an English and Classical School in Chicago in fall 1833 and Sarah L. Warren assisting him in March 1834. The source's Granville spelling is retained as a variant against the repository's Grenville spelling rather than silently normalized.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

PRINTED AGAINST THIS NAME IN THE 1833-1835 PRESS and carried here from the newspaper gazetteer (T-1254, by tools/derive_resident_roles.py). The gazetteer holds its trades on the PERSON record and not on a single issue, so the bound is the run of this person's own dated mentions, 1833-12-03 to 1834-02-25, and the grade is `inferred`: the paper printed the trade, and the resident programme's identity rule tied the printing to this card. The scene date falls outside that run, so this role does not stand in the 1835 view.

age_band.note: THE BAND THIS PERSON'S OWN BIRTH YEAR PUTS THEM IN on 1 July 1835. It is a view of a value already on this card and adds nothing to it; it exists so the age axis can be read across the whole layer at once, beside the bands the model draws for everybody else.

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as 'February 6, 1887' and the age as 'aged 79'. An age of 79 completed years means at least 79 and less than 80, so the birth falls between 1807-02-07 and 1808-02-06: the birth year is 1807 or 1808. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "Sproat, Granville Temple, school-teacher, died, Mt. Lebanon, N.Y., February 6, 1887, aged 79.", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

research_note: THE SCHOOLMASTER OF THE TOWN'S FIRST PURPOSE-BUILT SCHOOLROOM, and a household whose presence at the scene date is genuinely open. THE PARCEL'S SCHOOLING GAP IS WORTH STATING: in a town of 3,265 people this dataset can name three teachers - Watkins, Sproat and Eliza Chappel - of whom one is documented at work in the scene year, one is uncertain and one had married and left. George Davis, teaching on Lake Street in the winter of 1834-35 and in the Presbyterian church later in 1835, is a fourth and is the most obviously missing household in this parcel.

old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
